```sh
kafka scram delete <users...>
```

Delete a SCRAM credential for one or more users

## Arguments

| Argument   | Description                             |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `users...` | user names to delete the credential for |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Deletes credentials for the selected users/mechanism; other credentials are not a recovery copy.

## Before you run

Removes authentication material and can prevent new client connections. Recovery requires provisioning valid credentials again; the old password cannot be read back.

## Flags

| Flag                   | Description                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`   | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092   |
| `--mechanism <string>` | scram-sha-256 or scram-sha-512                     |
| `--yes`                | confirm the deletion without an interactive prompt |

## Examples

```sh
kafka scram delete alice --mechanism scram-sha-256 --brokers localhost:9092 --yes
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "results": []
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`, `5`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
